component: Current comparison capture and local measurement evidence
constraints: Inspect actual Python admission result objects and traced allocations alongside a separate Node primitive check on trusted local inputs; no service or physical transport.
Fixed six-case primitive corpus, five lexical checks, one 128-verification batch; input at most 64 KiB and retained stdout at most 4 KiB, with independently counted stderr.
alternatives: Python asyncio subprocess callbacks and independent Node crypto probe.
Node child_process orchestration with timeout/maxBuffer controls.
Rust Tokio process and pipe orchestration with explicit cleanup.
Java/Kotlin Process orchestration with streams, timeout and destruction.
rationale: KEEP direct Python observation for the interpreter-specific results and allocations. Other orchestrators can supervise the child but still need a Python observer and a typed report; no demonstrated correctness or deployment benefit warrants this boundary change.

Current Python subprocess transport documents pipe closure and direct child termination. Tokio documents explicit kill_on_drop and waiting requirements; Java warns that destruction need not complete immediately. These APIs all require cleanup reasoning; a language change alone supplies no hard deadline.

Fresh real-child tests verify byte-limit rejection, exit failure and timeout cleanup. A real Python/Node execution confirms six primitive results and five lexical rejections. Diagnostics explicitly deny runtime-ranking and target-hardware qualification. No implementation mismatch was found.
limits: Current source-based comparison, not executable parity or throughput benchmarking of alternative implementations. No preference based on installed tooling, familiarity or rewrite cost.
Before/after listed-file comparisons are not atomic, do not attest loaded code or dependency closure, and cannot detect transient changes restored between reads.
No hosted run, physical qualification, hard-real-time, MLS/CNSA, availability or complete-phase claim.
Exchange timeout excludes process creation and has separate cooperative cleanup; descendants, kernel buffers and total RSS are outside the guarantee.
Node implements primitive checks, not passport admission. Single local batches are not latency distributions, worst-case measurements or controlled statistical benchmarks.
